extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, regulated entities, state/tribal agencies, and stakeholders following federal rulemaking on water pollution control (Federal Register readers)
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register API search-results page listing documents (rules, proposed rules, notices) related to water-pollution-control. The page aggregates abstracts and basic metadata for many agency actions (EPA and others) relevant to Clean Water Act, CERCLA, and related programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic retention of Part 194 facility response plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend facility response plan regulations to allow operators of oil pipelines to keep electronic copies of onshore oil spill response plans or the "relevant portions" of those plans in lieu of paper copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change modifies existing regulatory retention requirements to allow electronic alternatives; applies to onshore oil pipeline operators maintaining response plans. (From: "Pipeline Safety: Electronic Retention of Part 194 Response Plans")

rubrics_metrics.name: National Priorities List (NPL) inclusion standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Under CERCLA, the NPL must include a list of national priorities among the known releases or threatened releases of hazardous substances, pollutants, or contaminants throughout the United States; the NPL is intended to guide EPA in determining which sites warrant further investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion on the NPL is based on known or threatened releases and is used to prioritize sites for further investigation to assess public health and environmental risks and to determine appropriate CERCLA-authorized remedial actions. (From: "National Priorities List")

rubrics_metrics.name: National Priorities List deletion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites may be deleted from the NPL where no further response is appropriate (per 40 CFR 300.425(e)); deletion does not preclude future Superfund actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deletion requires a determination that all appropriate response actions under CERCLA have been completed and that no further response is appropriate. Administrative corrections to NPL actions (e.g., name corrections) are also addressed. (From: "Deletion From the National Priorities List" and related notices)

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and modification of Ocean Dredged Material Disposal Sites (ODMDS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifications to expand designated boundaries of EPA-designated ocean dredged material disposal sites are proposed where needed to serve long-term disposal needs for suitable dredged material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modified ODMDS will be subject to monitoring and management to ensure continued protection of the marine environment; designation actions should consider long-term needs and environmental protection measures. (From: "Marine Protection: Modification To Expand Ocean Dredged Material Disposal Sites Offshore of Corpus Christi, Texas")

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage standard for Clean Water Act (CWA) Hazardous Substance Facility Response Plans (FRPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: FRP requirements apply to onshore non-transportation-related facilities that could reasonably be expected to cause substantial harm to the environment from a CWA hazardous substance worst case discharge to navigable waters, adjoining shorelines, or the exclusive economic zone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the universe of covered facilities for the CWA hazardous-substance FRP rule; agency actions (e.g., compliance-date delays) may affect timing and implementation for these covered facilities. (From: "Clean Water Act Hazardous Substance Facility Response Plans: Compliance Date Delay and Changes To Reflect Administration Policy")

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and implementation considerations for FRP compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may delay compliance dates or modify regulatory language to align with administration policy and to allow consideration of implementation and compliance-assistance tools for regulated parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delays are justified to permit development of implementation tools and to consider regulatory burden, but EPA notes uncertainties (e.g., inability to quantify number/nature/magnitude of covered discharges during a delay period). (From: same FRP delay/proposed rule notices)

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency reconsideration and amendment criteria for FRP rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance notice of proposed rulemaking seeks feedback on reconsidering FRP regulations to address implementation challenges and clarify requirements from prior final rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconsideration focuses on aligning with administration priorities, addressing regulatory burden where possible, while maintaining planning requirements to protect human health and the environment for CWA hazardous substance worst case discharges. (From: "Clean Water Act Hazardous Substance Facility Response Plans; Amendment Reconsideration")

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior notice requirements for citizen suits (electronic service)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revisions would generally require electronic service to EPA of Notices of Intent (NOIs) to file a citizen suit under multiple environmental statutes (CAA, CWA, SDWA, NCA, RCRA, CERCLA, TSCA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The change is intended to help ensure EPA receives and processes NOIs in a timely and efficient manner by standardizing and modernizing the manner in which prior notice is provided. (From: "Prior Notice of Citizen Suits")

rubrics_metrics.name: Water Quality Certification (CWA §401) substantive and procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule updates and clarifies several substantive and procedural requirements for water quality certification under Clean Water Act section 401; section 401 grants States (and eligible Tribes) authority to review compliance with appropriate water quality requirements for discharges into waters of the United States that may result from federally-licensed or permitted activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifications aim to make certification process aspects consistent with the statutory framework, improving predictability and clarifying who may act and how certifications should be processed. (From: "Updating the Water Quality Certification Regulations")

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Waters of the United States' (WOTUS) — scope and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision of regulations defining the scope of waters federally covered under the Federal Water Pollution Control Act (Clean Water Act), informed by Sackett v. EPA, with intent to provide greater regulatory certainty and increase program predictability and consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agencies intend the rule to clarify scope while respecting State and Tribal authority over their land and water resources and to implement the Clean Water Act objective to restore and maintain the quality of the Nation's waters. (From: "Updated Definition of 'Waters of the United States'")

rubrics_metrics.name: Effluent Limitations Guidelines (Steam Electric) — applicability and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals and direct-final actions address extensions of deadlines, updates to transfer provisions to allow facilities to switch between compliance alternatives, and authority for alternative applicability and paperwork submission dates based on site-specific factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency may withdraw direct final rules if adverse comments are received; stakeholder comment can influence deadlines, transferability between compliance alternatives, and site-specific applicability determinations. (From: multiple "Effluent Limitations Guidelines and Standards for the Steam Electric Power Generating" entries)

rubrics_metrics.name: Water quality standards to protect aquatic life (example: Delaware River DO criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalized designated use of protection and propagation of resident and migratory aquatic life and corresponding dissolved-oxygen (DO) water quality criteria for specified water-quality management zones of the mainstem Delaware River (river miles/zones specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WQS actions establish designated uses and numeric criteria (here, DO) for particular segments/zones; such standards are promulgated under the CWA to protect aquatic life and must be applied in permitting and water-quality management. (From: "Water Quality Standards To Protect Aquatic Life in the Delaware River")

rubrics_metrics.name: State program approval criteria for Underground Storage Tank (UST) programs
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA approves State UST program revisions when the State's statutes and regulations meet federal requirements for approval under RCRA Subtitle I; approved provisions are incorporated by reference and are subject to EPA inspection and enforcement authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval codifies the State program's authorized provisions and signals EPA will enforce those provisions; prior notices and opportunities for comment are part of the authorization process. (From: "Minnesota: Final Approval of State Underground Storage Tank Program Revisions, Codification, and Incorporation by Reference")
